USA_1970_F7.name: Israeli Security Aid
USA_1970_F7.description: A standing security-assistance programme gives both governments a practical relationship in training and defence supply. Industrial expansion remains a separate agreement requiring renewed Israeli consent.

USA_1970_E9.name: North American Trade
USA_1970_E9.description: Canada and Mexico each receive an independent proposal for industrial and commercial cooperation. Each government can accept or decline its own terms. Later supplier and border-industry investment remains a separate negotiation.

USA_1970_NIX_F3.name: Reassure the Alliances
USA_1970_NIX_F3.description: Washington offers an allied-readiness programme to countries holding recognised NATO membership or major non-NATO ally status. Each government decides independently. American coordination remains one national institution, with additional weekly funding for every participating partner.

hooks.membership_hook_scope: Country after native NATO/MNNA admission or removal; USA readmission performs a one-off dispatch

alliance_partner_pool: Any existing country holding NATO_member or Major_Non_NATO_Ally; no static tag whitelist
migration: Completed old roots authorise actual offers without setup fees or automatic spirits. Parent must retire their old legacy execution/retry bundles and remove old recurring helper deltas once, preserving historical payments.
implementation_notes: No sender offer selector. Offers originate in their distinct roots; recipient decisions can reopen authorised terms.
No new status, faction, military access, territorial transfer, equipment or building is granted.
Advanced existing agreements retain their own accepted terms and costs; attach the published parent guards in offer availability, acceptance and ongoing readiness.
